sections.h2: Where is Idaho Falls and how big is it?
sections.html:
Idaho Falls is the county seat of Bonneville County in eastern Idaho and the fourth most populous city in the state. It is also the most populous Idaho city outside the Boise area.

The Census Bureau estimates 71,785 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 64,818 at the 2020 census. The Idaho Falls metropolitan area counted 154,855 people in 2020. The city works as the commercial, cultural and health care hub for Eastern Idaho, with some pull from western Wyoming and southern Montana.

The Snake River runs through town, and the city sits at about 4,712 feet. That elevation matters for a house, which we cover in the climate section below.

sections.h2: What shaped Idaho Falls, and what pays the bills today?
sections.html:
Idaho Falls grew from a river crossing into a railroad town and then into a research and service center. The settlement began as Taylor's Crossing, became known as Eagle Rock by 1866, and took the name Idaho Falls in 1891 after the rapids below the bridge.

Irrigation made the surrounding valley productive farmland. The area grew sugar beets, potatoes, peas, grains and alfalfa, and agriculture still frames the region even though the city itself leans on other employers.

The largest single factor is the Idaho National Laboratory. The Atomic Energy Commission opened the National Reactor Testing Station in the desert west of town in 1949, and INL and its contractors now employ more than 8,000 people across the desert site and a research campus in Idaho Falls. Other institutions in town include the College of Eastern Idaho, the Museum of Idaho and the Idaho Falls Regional Airport.

sections.h2: What does the Idaho Falls climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Idaho Falls has a semi-arid climate with warm summers and cold winters, so heating, insulation and roof load matter more than cooling. Precipitation is sparse, but snow adds up.

Measure (airport station)Value
Average annual precipitation10.07 inches
Average annual snowfall36.9 inches
January mean daily minimum12.1 F
July mean daily maximum86.6 F
Record low-51 F
Record high103 F

Those figures come from National Weather Service and NOAA normals. A buyer's inspector in this climate will look at the furnace, attic insulation, window seals and anything that can freeze, such as exterior hose bibs and supply lines in crawl spaces.

Severe weather is uncommon. An F2 tornado hit the Idaho Falls area on April 7, 1978, and natural disasters are described as rare. Hail and wind claims on roofs are worth checking in your own insurance history before you list.

sections.h2: Which parts of Idaho Falls do buyers and sellers talk about?
sections.html:
Idaho Falls is usually described by a handful of areas, each with a different housing stock.

  • Downtown: the historic townsite on the east side of the river, home to the Museum of Idaho, the Colonial Theatre, the Art Museum of Eastern Idaho and the public library.
  • The Numbered Streets: the first planned neighborhood in the city, running between South Boulevard and Holmes Avenue, and including the Eleventh Street Historic District.
  • West Side: the area around the Idaho Falls Regional Airport.
  • Snake River Landing: a large mixed-use development west of the river near I-15, with residential space, restaurants, parks and the Mountain America Center.

The river walk, formerly called the Greenbelt, follows several miles of the Snake River and is maintained by the city. Older homes in the numbered streets area often carry the kind of deferred maintenance a cash buyer will price in, while newer subdivisions farther out tend to need less.

Idaho Falls School District 91 serves the city. It reports more than 10,000 students in 19 schools: 12 elementary, two middle and five high schools. School boundaries are worth confirming with the district if a buyer asks.

sections.h2: How do utilities work when you sell or move out in Idaho Falls?
sections.html:
Idaho Falls runs its own electric utility, so a move is handled through the city. Idaho Falls Power has served the city since 1900, and it owns five hydropower plants that supply about one-third of the city's electricity.

The city consolidates electric, water, sanitation and wastewater on one bill and handles starting, stopping or moving service in one place at City Hall, 308 Constitution Way. To close an account, you sign in to the customer self-service portal with your existing account.

One detail matters for houses with recent work. If you finish upgrades and need power turned back on, the work must be inspected by the city electrical inspectors at the Building Department. After the inspection passes, a connect order goes to Idaho Falls Power. A house with unpermitted electrical work can therefore stall a sale or a re-energizing, so ask the Building Division what is on file before you list.

  • Close or transfer service after the sale date is set, not before the buyer's final walkthrough.
  • Keep power and water on through closing so inspections and appraisals can happen.
  • Gather permit records for any panel, furnace or water heater changes.

sections.h2: What do Idaho Falls sellers owe the county, and when?
sections.html:
Property tax in Idaho Falls is billed by Bonneville County, not by the state. The Idaho State Tax Commission states that the State of Idaho does not receive any property tax. Counties levy and collect it for the cities, school districts and other taxing districts.

The county assessor estimates what a typical buyer would pay for your property as of January 1, at 100% of market value less exemptions. Idaho law does not cap year-to-year changes in value, although each taxing district can raise the property tax part of its budget by no more than 3% unless voters approve more or new construction and annexation add to the base.

WhenWhat happens (Bonneville County)
January 1Lien date used to set market value
April 15Last day to apply for the homeowner's exemption or property tax reduction for the year
First Monday in JuneAssessor mails assessment notices
Fourth Monday in JuneDeadline to appeal to the Board of Equalization
December 20Taxes due in full, or first half due
June 20Second half due if the first half was paid

The homeowner's exemption covers 50% of the value of your home and up to one acre, with a maximum of $125,000, and it lasts only until ownership changes or you stop using the home as your primary residence. The buyer will need to apply on their own, so expect your tax bill to look different from theirs. Ask the title company to prorate taxes at closing. If you disagree with a value, start with the assessor, then the Board of Equalization, then the State Board of Tax Appeals or district court within 30 days.

sections.h2: What must an Idaho Falls seller disclose?
sections.html:
Idaho requires most sellers of one to four unit residential property to complete a property condition disclosure form. The Property Condition Disclosure Act, Idaho Code 55-2504, covers sales, exchanges, installment contracts and options to buy, and it includes nonowner-occupied rental property.

Idaho Code 55-2505 lists exemptions. Among them are transfers by a fiduciary in administering a decedent's estate, transfers that result from foreclosure, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and transfers from a transferor who inherited the property and has not lived in it within the past year. If your sale falls in one of those groups, the form may not be required, but the safest path is to confirm with a licensed Idaho attorney or title officer.

In practice, disclosure is where as-is sales and listed sales differ. A listed buyer's inspector and lender may demand repairs after the form is signed. A direct cash purchase of the house in its present condition removes the repair negotiation, although the disclosure rules above still apply to the transfer itself.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of an Idaho Falls house usually run?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so the timeline depends on title work and the seller's schedule rather than on loan underwriting. You request an offer, the buyer reviews the house, and if you accept, a title or escrow company clears title, prepares documents and closes.

  • Share the address, condition, any liens or back taxes, and whether tenants occupy the house.
  • Compare the offer against listing costs, repair costs and holding costs such as utilities and taxes.
  • Choose a closing date that suits you. Closing is handled by a title company that also pays off any mortgage or tax balance from proceeds.

You owe nothing if you turn an offer down. Whether a cash offer beats a listing depends on your house, so get a second opinion from a local agent if you are unsure.

faqs.q: How many people live in Idaho Falls?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 71,785 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 64,818, and the wider metropolitan area had 154,855 people.

faqs.q: When are Bonneville County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due in full on December 20. If you pay at least half by then, the second half is due by June 20 of the following year, according to the Bonneville County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Do I have to fill out a disclosure form to sell my Idaho Falls house?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Idaho Code 55-2504 requires sellers of one to four unit residential property to complete a property condition disclosure form, with exemptions listed in 55-2505 such as estate transfers and some inherited homes.

faqs.q: How do I shut off utilities when I sell in Idaho Falls?
faqs.a: Sign in to the city's customer self-service portal with your existing account to close service. Idaho Falls handles electric, water, sanitation and wastewater together at City Hall, 308 Constitution Way.

faqs.q: Does the homeowner's exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The Idaho State Tax Commission says the exemption lasts until ownership changes or you stop living in the home as your primary residence, so the buyer applies separately with the county assessor.

faqs.q: What if my Idaho Falls house needs major repairs?
faqs.a: You can still sell it. Repairs usually slow a listing because buyers and lenders ask for fixes, while a cash buyer prices the condition into the offer. Compare both routes using your own repair estimates.
